database_summary: Small movie dataset (SQLite) with core entities: movies, names (people), genres, director and role mappings, and ratings. movies holds one row per film with descriptive attributes; names holds one row per person. genre, director_mapping, role_mapping are many-to-many bridge/event tables linking movies and people/genres. ratings contains per-movie aggregated rating measures. Row counts: movies 7,997; names 25,735; genre 14,662; role_mapping 15,615; director_mapping 3,867; ratings 7,997.

accepted.name: movies_basic
accepted.body_sql: SELECT id, title, year, date_published, duration, country, worlwide_gross_income, languages, production_company FROM movies
accepted.description: One-row-per-movie projection selecting core descriptive columns from movies. Use to filter cohorts of movies by year, country, production_company, duration, or languages before joining to other tables. | Use for: List movies released in a given year or year range; Filter movies by country or production_company; Find movies longer/shorter than a duration threshold; Prepare a cohort of movies for aggregation or joins

accepted.name: movies_with_ratings
accepted.body_sql: SELECT m.id, m.title, m.year, m.date_published, m.duration, m.country, m.worlwide_gross_income, m.languages, m.production_company, r.avg_rating, r.total_votes, r.median_rating FROM movies m LEFT JOIN ratings r ON m.id = r.movie_id
accepted.description: Denormalized one-row-per-movie combining movies and ratings. Useful for analyses that need movie attributes plus avg_rating, total_votes, and median_rating without further joins. | Use for: Rank or filter movies by avg_rating or total_votes; Compute correlations between movie attributes and ratings; List top-rated movies with their metadata

accepted.name: movie_genres
accepted.body_sql: SELECT movie_id, TRIM(genre) AS genre FROM genre
accepted.description: Normalized one-row-per (movie, genre) assignment with trimmed genre values. Use when you need a clean genre roster for each movie for grouping or filtering. | Use for: Count movies per genre; Filter movies that belong to a given genre; Join genres to movie metadata for genre-level aggregations

accepted.name: movie_directors_with_names
accepted.body_sql: SELECT dm.movie_id, dm.name_id, n.name, n.height, n.date_of_birth, n.known_for_movies FROM director_mapping dm LEFT JOIN names n ON dm.name_id = n.id
accepted.description: One-row-per director assignment enriched with director name attributes. Join director_mapping to names to find directors' names and attributes for each movie. | Use for: List directors (names) for a movie or set of movies; Aggregate number of movies per director; Filter directors by date_of_birth or height

accepted.name: movie_cast_with_names
accepted.body_sql: SELECT rm.movie_id, rm.name_id, rm.category, n.name, n.height, n.date_of_birth, n.known_for_movies FROM role_mapping rm LEFT JOIN names n ON rm.name_id = n.id
accepted.description: One-row-per cast membership (role_mapping) enriched with person attributes from names. Preserve role category to allow actor/actress filtering and counts per movie. | Use for: Count cast members per movie or by category; Find movies featuring a given actor/actress; Compute average actor height per movie

accepted.name: movies_genre_counts
accepted.body_sql: SELECT g.movie_id AS id, COUNT(*) AS genre_count FROM genre g GROUP BY g.movie_id
accepted.description: One-row-per-movie aggregated count of associated genres. Useful for filtering movies by how many genres they are tagged with or for join-safe summaries. | Use for: Find movies with multiple genres; Filter movies by genre_count before further analysis; Join genre_count to movies to analyze multi-genre films

accepted.name: movie_rating_rank
accepted.body_sql: SELECT r.movie_id AS movie_id, r.avg_rating AS avg_rating, r.total_votes AS total_votes, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY r.avg_rating DESC, r.total_votes DESC) AS rating_rank FROM ratings r
accepted.description: Ranking of movies by avg_rating within the whole dataset. Produces a dense rank so downstream queries can select top-K by filtering rank <= K. Use after joining to movies metadata if needed. | Use for: Select top-K movies by avg_rating (filter rating_rank <= K); Compare ranks across rating and vote-count dimensions

accepted.name: names_basic
accepted.body_sql: SELECT id, name, height, date_of_birth, known_for_movies FROM names
accepted.description: One-row-per-person projection of the names table with common attributes. Use for filtering people by name, date_of_birth, height, or known_for_movies before joining to role/director mappings. | Use for: List people with certain birth dates or height ranges; Find people known for specific movies; Prepare person cohorts for role or director analyses
